motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Rezone for Stonebridge Montessori. Mr. Mumford presented the item. The Ranches Master Development Plan has expired, thus a rezone is required. The Future Land Use Plan designation for the location is Community Commercial. The CC and CN zones are appropriate within the General Plan designation. Staff had recommended the building be turned 90 degrees to front along Ranches Parkway with the parking located behind the building. The Planning Commission supported the layout submitted by the applicant as it increases student safety. A three-and-a-half-foot headlight screen is required east and south of the parking lot. Originally staff requested a lane on the west side of the property extend north and connect to an access road on the neighboring property, as a master site plan and preliminary plat were approved for the northern property in 2008 for Saddle Junction, but has not been constructed. The applicant expressed safety concerns for the students should the northern connection be required. The road would benefit future projects but not the school. Should the road not be required for this project, it would need to be constructed entirely on the project to the west. The front entry faces towards the parking lot, not a main pedestrian way, as called for by EMMC 17.72.040(B). It is at the discretion of the City Council to determine if the articulation provided complies with standards found in EMMC 17.72.040(D). The Planning Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the rezone with the condition that the property be rezoned to the Commercial Neighborhood (CN) rather than the Commercial Community (CC) zone. The Planning Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the site plan with the following conditions: 1. The site plan shall be approved without a drive-aisle connecting the northern property; 2. The applicant shall provide proof that the stacking distances are adequate and will not cause traffic to back onto public right-of-way; 3. A 3½-foot high landscape berm shall be added around the perimeter of the parking area; and 4. The applicant shall provide additional directional signs in the parking lot. Applicant representative Tyler Dow confirmed that the coffee room indicated on the site plan was a breakroom for staff rather than a retail store. He explained he was building the school for a lessee that has run other Montessori schools. The multisensory educational practices at this location would follow the same model. Traffic attendants will be on site to help with pedestrian safety, traffic flow, and stacking. A right-in turn is anticipated to provide onsite stacking rather than the two-directional traffic flow indicated on the site plan. The staggered start times for the classes should reduce the traffic congestion. The area in the southeast corner of the plan is a stormwater detention area. City Engineer Chris Trusty said the school access is spaced away from Ranches Parkway and the applicant has attempted to accommodate sufficient stacking distances to avoid traffic backing onto Ranches Parkway
